brief: 6 writing tips for founders who hate writing.

slots.headline: Six No-Nonsense Writing Tips for Founders Who Hate Writing

slots.title: Talk, Don't Type
slots.body: Record yourself explaining the idea, then transcribe the audio. Your natural speaking voice is clearer and more persuasive than forced prose. Edit the raw transcript into clean, readable copy.

slots.title: Brutal Outlines First
slots.body: Before you write, list the three bullet points you want the reader to remember. Expand each bullet into a single tight paragraph. This keeps your argument logical and easy to follow.

slots.title: Embrace the Ugly Draft
slots.body: Perfectionism kills momentum. Give yourself permission to write a terrible first draft without stopping to fix a single sentence. You can always polish garbage, but you cannot polish a blank page.

slots.title: Slash Your Word Count
slots.body: Founders often overwrite to sound authoritative. Remove every adverb and piece of jargon, then rewrite what remains in plain English. Clarity builds trust far faster than complexity ever will.

slots.title: Steal Proven Structures
slots.body: Stop inventing new formats from scratch. Use timeless templates like problem-agitation-solution or story-lesson-action. Familiar structures remove the intimidation of a blank page and speed up your workflow.

slots.title: Ship Before Ready
slots.body: Publish before you feel completely ready. Consistent writing beats perfect writing because public feedback teaches you faster than months of private practice ever could.
